semantics.note: The normalization preserves the reliability warning and both qualifiers: increasing complexity and distance from training data.

contract.note: Contemporary, unaided execution is a fair reading of the discussion. Requiring measured distribution shifts preserves an explicit qualifier. June 2025 and the operational meaning of dependable execution are reasonable interpretations.

evidence.note: Reports contemporary complexity-related execution failures, but does not measure training-distribution distance. It informs one component without establishing the contracted outcome.
Authentic earlier research documents generalization failures and prompting improvements. Its 2022 models do not establish reliability for the June 2025 target period.

Shows generalization is possible under specified theoretical and experimental conditions. This challenges a universal impossibility reading, but does not establish dependable execution by the contemporary models at issue.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents complexity-related failures but lacks measured departures from the contemporary models' training distributions. Earlier failures and conditional generalization successes settle neither the combined reliability warning nor its opposite under the fair contract.
